study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To expand a repository of normative models to include structural surface area and functional connectivity, and to compare the performance of normative modeling features (deviation scores) against raw data features in group difference testing, classification, and regression benchmarks.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: For functional models: A combination of 40 sites including ABCD, CAMCAN, CMI-HBN, HCP-Aging, HCP-Development, HCP-Early Psychosis, HCP-Young Adult, NKI-RS, OpenNeuro, PNC, and UKBiobank. For structural models (cortical thickness): a repository from Rutherford et al., 2022a. For surface area models: a similar combination of datasets as the functional models.
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper explicitly lists the datasets used for the functional models in Appendix 1 and Supplementary File 1. It refers to a previous publication for the cortical thickness models and provides a supplementary file for the surface area models.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Datasets used for training the functional normative models closely match the sample included in Rutherford et al., 2022a... The full details of the data included in the functional normative model training can be found in Appendix 1 and Supplementary file 1. ... We also share models of surface area, extracted in the same manner as the cortical thickness data from a similar dataset (described in Supplementary file 2).
rci1_dataset_name.location: Rutherford2023.pdf.md: Methods, Dataset selection and scanner parameters; Image preprocessing

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Structural: Freesurfer (v6.0) recon-all. Functional: fMRIPrep, followed by nuisance regression (WM/CSF, AROMA, motion).
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The preprocessing pipelines are clearly described in the Methods section.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Structural MRI data were preprocessed using the Freesurfer (version 6.0) recon-all pipeline... Resting-state data were preprocessed separately for each study using fMRIPrep...

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Structural: Visual inspection, successful Freesurfer execution, and Euler number thresholding (rescaled Euler < 10). Functional: High-quality structural scan required, >5min of low motion data (framewise displacement < 0.5 mm), and manual visual inspection.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: High-quality was defined for structural images as in our prior work ( Rutherford et al., 2022a ), namely as the lack of any artifacts such as ghosting or ringing, that Freesurfer surface reconstruction was able to run successfully, and that the Euler number calculated from Freesurfer ( Klapwijk et al., 2019 ), which is a proxy metric for scan quality, was below a chosen threshold (rescaled Euler <10) ( Kia et al., 2022 ). High-quality functional data followed recommended practices ( Siegel et al., 2017 ) and was defined as having a high-quality structural MRI (required for co-registration and normalization) and at least 5 min of low motion data (framewise displacement <0.5 mm).
rci8_quality_checking.location: Rutherford2023.pdf.md: Methods, Dataset selection and scanner parameters

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Site was included as a fixed-effects covariate in the Bayesian Linear Regression models for both structural and functional data.

The covariates used to train the functional normative models were similar to the structural normative models which included age, sex, data quality metric (mean framewise displacement), and site.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Mass univariate group difference testing (two-sample independent t-tests with FDR correction); multivariate classification (Support Vector Classification with linear kernel in 10-fold cross-validation); multivariate regression (Principal Component Regression / Brain Basis Set).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling features (deviation scores) consistently outperform raw data features in group difference testing, classification, and regression benchmarks, with the strongest benefits seen in detecting group differences for schizophrenia and classification.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: In mass univariate group difference testing for schizophrenia, normative models found numerous significant differences (117/187 cortical thickness regions, 50/136 functional connections) after FDR correction, while no significant differences were found using raw data. In classification, cortical thickness deviation scores achieved a significantly higher AUC (0.87) compared to raw data (0.43). For predicting general cognitive ability, deviation scores showed a modest, non-significant improvement in mean squared error.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The functional connectivity models use a low-resolution parcellation (Yeo-17), ignoring more complex aspects of brain dynamics. The demographic makeup of the training cohort is likely over-representative of European-ancestry populations (WEIRD), limiting generalizability. The term 'normative' is used in a purely statistical sense and does not imply a moral or ethical judgment.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, the representation of functional normative models may be surprising and concerning... We would also like to expand on our prior discussion ( Rutherford et al., 2022a ) on the limitations of the reference cohort demographics, and the use of the word 'normative.' The included sample for training the functional normative models in this work, and the structural normative modeling sample in Rutherford et al., 2022a are most likely overrepresentative of European-ancestry (WEIRD population Henrich et al., 2010 )... The term 'normative model' can be defined in other fields in a very different manner than ours... Critically, we do not use normative in a moral or ethical sense...

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study provides a user-friendly web portal (https://pcnportal.dccn.nl/) to allow researchers to apply the pre-trained models to their own data without programming.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The paper's central contribution is not just the new models, but a comprehensive benchmarking analysis that provides strong evidence for the advantages of using normative modeling outputs (deviation scores) over traditional preprocessed data for downstream clinical analyses.
